sections.text: 2.11 Design of Hydraulic Cylinder Piston Rod Hydrostatic Support Structure
1. General

The working principle of the piston rod hydrostatic support structure (hydraulic hydrostatic sliding bearing guiding the piston rod) is that the support force on the piston rod is mainly generated by external pressurized oil, rather than generated by the relative motion between the piston rod and its hydrostatic support sleeve (i.e., hydrodynamic effect).

The hydraulic hydrostatic bearing shaft in the sliding bearing guides the piston rod to reciprocate while bearing the loads acting on the piston rod. The piston rod hydrostatic support structure discussed in this manual includes the hydrostatic sliding bearing guiding the piston rod and its sliding contact components.

Generally, the design of piston rod hydrostatic support structures should follow these principles: under the maximum load that may be encountered, the minimum oil film thickness should at least maintain lubricating oil film thickness of 50%~60%.

In design, the eccentricity ratio (where the load eccentricity is the relative eccentricity ratio e = e/C₀) is limited to e = 0~0.5 in the range; the flow rate designed for the medium should be the set flow rate. This is because the hydrostatic support's ability to compensate for special eccentricity is at its strongest. It is also necessary to consider the hydrostatic support structure's load-bearing capacity, and there must be sufficient consideration for the forces acting in the oil cavity due to oil and the load acting on the oil cavity surface due to tightening, as well as the situation of reduced rigidity. It is especially important to note that one type of phenomenon is the eccentricity of the piston rod bending deflection leading to an offset from the center, and in the case of the piston rod hydrostatic support sleeve edge contact friction type hydrostatic support structure.

The design and calculation of the piston rod hydrostatic support structure is established on the basis of static (including front and boundary condition requirements). Whether enough determination of its operating parameters and operating conditions, geometry and shape, oil supply capacity, eccentricity ratio, load-bearing capacity, oil temperature and other functional relationships, as well as oil supply pressure, flow rate, friction power, temperature rise and other parameters, often needs to be verified by actual machines.
2. Structural Types

In common piston rod hydrostatic support bearing designs, the hydrostatic support sleeve has oil grooves between them, with 4 oil cavities or more (even number of cavities). The oil cavity depth is the groove depth (diameter direction C₀) 10 times or more, and the length-to-diameter ratio B/D is 0.3~1. This is the most commonly used structural type for this application.

This type, with and without oil return grooves, has a similar structure; under the same return oil pressure conditions, the type without oil return grooves requires a larger oil supply flow rate. 3. Basic Parameters

The basic parameters of piston rod hydrostatic support structure include: hydrostatic support sleeve inner diameter D₁, outer diameter D₀, width B, number of oil cavities Z, axial oil seal strip width b₁, circumferential oil seal strip width b₂, oil return groove width, oil cavity depth, oil return groove depth (equivalent to the bearing return pressure), and throttle type (such as small orifice throttle type, capillary tube type, internal feedback type, etc.). Refer to page 5.
4. Materials

Hydrostatic support sleeve (i.e., bearing sleeve) material: cast alloy conforms to the requirements of GB/T 18324-2001; cast copper alloy conforms to JB/T 7921-1995 requirements; forged copper alloy conforms to JB/T 7922-1995 requirements.

7) Contamination resistance: The electro-hydraulic servo valve should not deteriorate in performance (higher than) GB/T 14039 specified -/17/14 level contamination under normal working conditions.

Per GJB 3370-1998, for armored plate type electro-hydraulic servo valves, performance testing, acceptance testing, internal and external sealing oil pressure test, the servo valve fluid contamination level acceptance should not be higher than GJB 420 6/A level, the intercepted water content should not be higher than 7/A level, while the other test station fluid contamination level should not be higher than 8/A level. 8) Filtration precision: The electro-hydraulic servo valve should be used with a filter at the inlet port (pressure oil port) with a filtration precision of not less than 10μm.
The electro-hydraulic servo valve, when used for long service life, should have a filter at the inlet oil port with a filtration precision of not less than 5μm.

When conducting electro-hydraulic servo valve testing, it is recommended to install as close as possible to the electro-hydraulic servo valve inlet port (pressure oil port) location a filter with a filtration precision of 3μm.

9) External sealing: The electro-hydraulic servo valve under all types of specified operating conditions and during the entire working period should not have obvious external leakage (allow seepage, do not allow dripping).

(6) Environmental Requirements for Electro-hydraulic Servo Valves

1) Low temperature starting: The electro-hydraulic servo valve at ambient temperature and working temperature averaging -30°C, should be able to start with ±50% of rated current, and its seal should not have obvious external leakage (allow seepage, do not allow dripping).

2) High and low temperature: The electro-hydraulic servo valve at ambient temperature and working fluid temperature range of -30~135(90)°C, the rated flow deviation should not exceed ±25%, the resolution should not exceed 2% or the hysteresis should not exceed 6%. At high temperature the insulation resistance should be no less than 5MΩ, and its seal should not have obvious external leakage (allow seepage, do not allow dripping).
Per GB/T 13854 requirements (for high and low temperature), the servo valve operates at -30~60°C ambient temperature and working fluid at -30~90°C.
Per JB/T 10205, the high temperature test for the working oil of the electro-hydraulic servo valve should reach 90°C.

3) Temperature shock: The electro-hydraulic servo valve should comply with Figure 2-101 requirements. The temperature shock consists of 3 cycles of alternation, with insulation resistance no less than 5MΩ, zero drift no greater than 2% (jet pipe type zero drift no greater than 1.5%).

sections.description: A temperature-time graph showing temperature shock test profile. The y-axis shows temperature from -30±3 to 90±5°C, and the x-axis shows time in minutes. The profile shows rapid transitions between high temperature (90±5°C) and low temperature (-30±3°C) with hold periods of approximately 5 minutes at each extreme, connected by ramp transitions of approximately 5 minutes each. The cycle shows transitions at approximately 60-minute intervals.

3) Requirements for finished products:

items: 1) The outer surface of the product should be free of nickel layer, coating and anodized layer deposits. Mark one layer of anti-rust cast iron (or anti-rust coating).

2) Packaging should be dust-proof and moisture-proof, and should be processed through established procedures with proper anti-corrosion sand (1kg/m³) and moisture-indicating strips (or indicator paper).

sections.text: 4) Assembly requirements
Pre-assembly inspection should be carried out as follows:

items: a. Component manufacturing should conform to QJ 1499 requirements, with no burrs, scratches, and surface treatment with a complete layer.
b. Components should be cleaned, and visual inspection should show no visible contamination.
c. Rubber seals and rubber-metal composite parts should be free of pores, discoloration, blistering, aging, and cracking defects.

d. Certificates of conformity should match actual products. Component storage periods and validity dates of inspection should be within the prescribed period. For rubber parts installed in working fluid immersion for 24 hours, care should be taken to install seals with their sealing and pressing directions correct.

Note: "Pre-assembly rubber parts should be placed in working fluid for soaking 24h" was derived from QJ 2478-1993 specification; the author considers this may not be a good practice and suggests that hydraulic cylinder assembly should not use this process method.
e. Hydraulic products and their components during assembly should represent the actual working conditions.
f. During assembly, threaded connecting parts (where work permits graduation marks can be removed) should have external thread surfaces conforming to SY 1510 with No. 12 thread sealant applied.
g. During assembly testing, tools, fixtures, or threaded fasteners are allowed to cause the assembly surface layer to undergo slight breakage, but should not damage the base metal surface.

h. Products disassembled include springs, spring washers, rubber and plastic O-rings, shaped rubber washers, laminated rubber seals and gaskets (including polytetrafluoroethylene material backing rings, gasket washers, etc.). When reassembling, these should not be reused; they must be replaced with new parts.

i. Product assembly should ensure completeness. Components should have interchangeability (unless the drawing indicates selective assembly or matching). Components should not be allowed to undergo further cutting after assembly.

sections.text: Processing: Electronic product assembly, test leads and lead-out wires, should be assembled according to QJ 165 and special technical requirements.

When connecting internal leads, the wire should use nylon or linen thread for binding. The leads should be secured by the metal mesh guard, and joints with metal substrates should be properly insulated.

2.17.2 Specific Technical Requirements for Hydraulic Cylinder Assembly Fixtures
1. Assembly Preparation

items: 1) Prepare production instructions, arrange good tooling, have complete technical data and work instruction documents.
2) Carry out assembly according to specifications, follow the assembly drawing with detailed and clear notes on all single-use materials described below for spare parts. Parts.

3) Inspection: Parts that are the main assembled fit parts, using a method of trial assembly, can directly check parts for fit, carry out acceptance, inspection of exterior surface dimensions, ensuring that parts entering the assembly process are qualified, guaranteeing no defective parts are used.
4) Trial operation of adjustment and verification of machine tool flexibility should be tested for each working point.

5) Important: Component work surface and mating surface must not have burrs, scratches, bruises, corrosion, rust, and ring damage. All seals (including dust seals, O-rings, support rings, etc.) with damage marks should not be used.
6) Verify: Perform cleaning of the assembly area to remove dirt and debris. Drawings should indicate no further processing.
7) Cleaning: Perform cleaning of each component, and submit clean work report including all cleaning documentation.
8) Cleaned components should be placed in separate areas, then cleaned again and maintained.

9) Assembly sequence: Components should be completed before proceeding to assembly. Components should be used with assembly materials (adhesives), components should be wrapped (covered) for packaging and storage.

sections.text: 2. Assembly
(1) General technical requirements for seal component assembly.
The function of seals is to prevent leakage or rapid measurement. A reasonable assembly effort and method can improve seal durability (service life).

Installation sequence for each component: specifically for each type of seal, such as shaft seals (e.g., piston rod seals), chamfer seals (e.g., flat gaskets), dust seals (e.g., no burrs, flash, flying edges, etc.), and all components (including components with backing and mating surfaces) should have no tool marks (such as hacksaw marks, abrasive cloth marks, grinding/file marks), cut marks, nicks, abrasion marks, etc.

Assembly parts should be inspected and confirmed for all components, with low-value consumables and other equal quality standards as the acceptance criteria. Organize the assembly in detailed sequence.
